purpose: Teach: ウキウキ/なんにも/おこる/ひと時/概して/めんどう/こまかい/やむを得ず

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが旅の前にウキウキされたぞ
lines.en: When you were young, your father used to light up before a trip, didn't he.
lines.style: Soft, reminiscent voice. Gentle certainty in the memory — not a question, a shared recollection. Slow, measured pace. Eyes looking toward something distant and held.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、苦しい時もなんにも仰らないお方でらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes — your grandfather was such a quiet man about his troubles, wasn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm agreement with a gentle correction underneath. Talking to her husband across decades of knowing him. Soft cadence on the endearment. Not correcting — supplementing his memory with her own.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがおこるかどうかひやひやしたぞ
lines.en: When you were young, I used to worry whether your father would get angry or not.
lines.style: Slower now, touching something more vulnerable. The memory carries a small anxiety even in recollection. Pause before the anxiety admission — checking if it's safe to say aloud after all these years.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お孫様と、ひと時を大事になさったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather was so careful to treasure those moments with his grandchildren, wasn't he, dear?
lines.style: Affirming and gentle. Speaking to what he valued most, even if he didn't say it. Her voice holds pride in this observation. Warm, steady — the voice of someone who watched him closely and loved what she saw.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは概して穏やかでらしたぞ
lines.en: When you were young, your father was generally a very calm man.
lines.style: Reflective and still. The certainty of long years of living alongside someone. Quiet acknowledgment of a fundamental quality. Trailing slightly at the end — letting the fact sit.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、書類整理がめんどうでらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: But he found paperwork such a nuisance, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Gentle affection in the small complaint. A laugh lives underneath — the memory of his impatience with mundane tasks. Her voice softens on the 'dear' — intimacy built from knowing someone's small annoyances better than their virtues.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんはこまかい所まで気を配られたぞ
lines.en: When you were young, your father paid such careful attention to the smallest details.
lines.style: Proud recognition. Voice lands firmly on the care he took. Acknowledging something he perhaps never received credit for. Held, respectful — the observation of someone who noticed what he did.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、晩年は、やむを得ず病院通いだったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: In his later years, he had no choice but to make those hospital visits so often, didn't he, dear.
lines.style: Softer now, the inevitability of aging settling in the voice. Not sad — factual and held. The endearment carries particular tenderness here, anchoring them both in a shared acceptance.
